title: Full-stack generation (frontend + backend + middleware)
intro: Driven by one shared API contract: the frontend, backend and middleware pipelines generate concurrently, then deploy atomically into a live preview where the frontend calls the real backend.
needFlowHint: The development flow isn't complete yet — finish the requirements and flow before generating the full-stack app.
waitingAll: Deploy becomes available once the pipelines finish — the backend project must succeed (the frontend and middleware are best-effort).
backendRequired: The backend project must finish successfully before you can deploy. Retry the backend pipeline, then deploy.
deployDespiteFailure: Some pipelines didn't finish cleanly, but the backend is ready, so you can still deploy — the database setup or live frontend preview may be incomplete.
deployHint: The backend project is ready. Run the atomic deploy (create database → build backend image → start container → health check → wire the reverse proxy).
redeployHint: Re-run the deploy + auto-repair cycle on the existing projects — no need to regenerate the frontend/backend.
regenerateBackendHint: Regenerate only the backend project (reuses the frozen contract; the frontend/middleware stay untouched). Then re-deploy to rebuild and run the repair cycle.
apiBase: The frontend calls the backend live via {{base}}.

toast.started: Full-stack generation started (frontend / backend / middleware concurrently)

repairedTooltip: Deploy auto-fixed {{count}} backend file(s) to match the contract — download the repaired source (this is what the running app was built from).

git.branchHint: The platform overwrites the {{main}} branch with each validated snapshot; do your secondary development on the {{dev}} branch.
git.devNote: The {{dev}} branch is yours — the platform never touches it, so your changes are never overwritten.
